newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end firmer but buyers cautious.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end firmer but buyers cautious.

text.p: Australian shares bounced to a firmer close on Monday after being dumped on Friday following cautionary comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 25.9 points up at 2,339.8, not far from its intra-session high of 2,344.7.

The market was cautiously bid from the open after the Dow averted a major sell-off on Friday due to a subdued November payrolls report which eased U.S. investor fears that the Fed could raise short term interest rates.
"The bounce came in the first 30 minutes and then the market just crawled sideways on fairly thin volume," a dealer from a Brisbane-based brokerage said.
The dealer said most buying activity was contained within the bank sector which was hardest-hit by selling on Friday.
"This time of the year investors are looking for a steady rise to the new year - any sign that this is not going to happen usually just keeps them out of the market," he said.
The dealer said that if Wall Street rebounded tonight this would provide a stronger incentive for bargain hunters to buy in anticipation of further gains towards the new year.

Three of Australia's four major banks were in the 10 most active stocks by value on the day, all ending with good gains. The most active stock was bellwether resource issue, BHP, which closed 16 cents higher at A$17.64 (US$14.11).
